focus: Trace worktree base and provisioning inputs, Commit-Id opt-in, and shared allocator/hook behavior
keyQuestions: How do worktree naming/provisioning, Commit-Id allocation, hook trust, global hooks, and preflight advice interact?
noveltyJustification: Worktree location, provisioning inputs, Commit-Id policy, and allocator/enforcement failure paths add new repository adaptation surfaces.

label: Worktree base is repository-configurable through SPECKIT_WORKTREE_BASE or speckit.worktreeBase, with environment-first precedence and .worktrees fallback; setup should report the effective resolved base and compare it with registered worktrees.

worktree-provision-paths.txt is the repository-owned package/build-output inventory; a read-only check can verify the list, package paths, and declared outputs but cannot establish that future dependency installation or builds will succeed.

Local skilled.commitId true/false overrides Commit-Id autodetection; false disables stamping and the required-trailer check, although the shipped author template still presents Commit-Id as mandatory.

Commit-Id allocation is a seven-digit shared sequence across linked worktrees; a missing helper/allocator or failed stamp leaves the message unstamped, and commit-msg blocks a missing required ID, so setup should inspect policy, allocator, and installed hooks separately.
